segments.text: Transnational crime requires information-sharing, training, standards and cross-border cooperation.

INTERPOL supports police cooperation and notices; EUROPOL supports EU law-enforcement cooperation; UNODC works on drugs, crime, corruption, terrorism and justice; UNICEF is relevant especially to child protection; UNAFEI focuses on crime prevention and criminal justice training/research.

INTERPOL is an intergovernmental police-cooperation organization with 196 member countries. It enables national police to exchange information, use global databases and coordinate through National Central Bureaus. It is not a supranational police force with a general power to enter a country and make arrests.

Operational coercive authority remains with national agencies under domestic law. INTERPOL notices and data-sharing tools support cooperation; they do not by themselves replace extradition, arrest warrants or national legal process.

blocks.text: UNODC, UNICEF, UNAFEI and regional bodies

segments.text: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime supports states on transnational organized crime, drugs, corruption, terrorism prevention and criminal justice. UNICEF’s role is especially relevant where justice systems affect children, including protection, diversion and child-sensitive procedures. UNAFEI provides training and research in crime prevention and criminal justice.

Europol supports law-enforcement cooperation among EU member states; its mandate is regional rather than global. Professional associations such as the International Police Association serve different networking or professional purposes and should not be confused with treaty-based law-enforcement bodies.

Use four questions: What is the organization’s legal basis? Which countries or institutions participate? Does it collect intelligence, coordinate operations, train personnel, set standards or investigate? Does it itself possess coercive power?
This comparison prevents the common mistake of calling every international security body a “world police.”

items.text: International policing cooperation exists because criminals, money, data, drugs and victims can cross borders while police powers remain primarily national.
INTERPOL provides channels, databases and notice systems that help member-country police cooperate; it does not operate as an independent global arrest force.

EUROPOL supports law-enforcement cooperation within the European Union; UNODC supports international work on drugs, organized crime, corruption, terrorism and criminal justice; UNAFEI focuses on training and research; UNICEF contributes especially to child protection and justice for children.
For each organization prepare mandate, geographic scope, core tools and one limitation. This prevents a vague list of abbreviations.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not say an international organization can automatically arrest a suspect inside Pakistan. Operational authority remains governed by domestic law and international cooperation procedures.

items.text: Prepare mandate, membership/scope and one function for each.
Do not say INTERPOL is a global police force with independent arrest powers.
